Adjusting for both hospital and severity gives an ATE of about −5.09 days. The drug shortens hospital stays by roughly 5 days.

Hospital is a confounder because it determines both the chance of getting the drug (90% versus 10%) and how severe patients are. Severity is measured before treatment and strongly predicts days hospitalised, so including it is valid and makes the estimate more precise.

I ran the regression `days ~ treatment + hospital + severity`:

| Adjustment | Treatment coefficient |
|---|---|
| None | +14.15 (misleading, because of confounding) |
| Hospital only | −10.80 |
| Hospital and severity | −5.09 |

The hospital-only model is also a valid choice, since treatment is randomised within each hospital. I went with the fuller model because it uses severity, which explains much of the variation in days.

ANSWER: -5.09
